record.paper_title: Some Open Problems Concerning Orthogonal Polynomials on Fractals and Related Questions
record.original_question: Characterize which asymptotic growth rates of the Markov factors M_n(K) mark the boundary of the so-called zone of uncertainty for the extension property of a compact set K. In other words, determine the growth regimes of Markov's factors that separate cases where the extension property is forced from cases where it fails or is not determined by those growth rates.

evidence.quote: Problem 4. Characterize the growth rates of Markov’s factors that define the boundaries of the zone of uncertainty for the extension property.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a compact set with $|K| > 1$. For each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, define the $n$-th Markov factor of $K$ by
$$M_n(K) = \sup\Big\{\frac{\|P'\|_K}{\|P\|_K} : P \text{ a polynomial of degree at most } n,\ P\not\equiv 0\Big\},$$
where $\|\cdot\|_K$ denotes the supremum norm on $K$. Let $\mathcal{E}(K)$ denote the space of Whitney jets on $K$. The set $K$ is said to have the extension property if there exists a continuous linear operator $W : \mathcal{E}(K) \to C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$ such that $(Wf)|_K = f$ for every $f \in \mathcal{E}(K)$.

It is known that:
(i) if $M_n(K)$ grows at most polynomially in $n$ (i.e., $K$ has Markov's property), then $K$ has the extension property; and
(ii) there exist compact sets $K$ for which $M_n(K)$ grows faster than any polynomial yet $K$ still has the extension property, as well as compact sets with comparable growth of $M_n(K)$ for which the extension property fails. The intermediate growth regimes form what is called the "zone of uncertainty."

Problem: Characterize precisely the asymptotic growth rates of $\bigl(M_n(K)\bigr)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ that delineate the boundaries of this zone of uncertainty — that is, identify the threshold growth rates that separate the regime in which the extension property is forced to hold (or to fail) from the regime in which the growth of $M_n(K)$ alone does not determine whether $K$ has the extension property.
artifact.category_tag: Markov factors and Whitney extension property
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of characterizing the boundaries of the zone of uncertainty for the extension property in terms of growth of Markov's factors appears to remain open. Progress reports by Goncharov (2017) note that the extension property cannot be characterized solely in terms of growth of Markov's factors, and constructions of compact sets without Markov's property but with the extension property show the zone is genuinely nontrivial; no complete characterization of its boundaries is known.

status_evidence.title: Mityagin's extension problem. Progress report (Goncharov)
status_evidence.snippet: The extension property cannot be characterized in terms of growth of Markov's factors for the set.
status_evidence.claim: As of this progress report, no characterization of the extension property via growth of Markov's factors is known, indicating the boundaries of the zone of uncertainty remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A compact set without Markov's property but with an extension operator for C^infty-functions (Goncharov)
status_evidence.snippet: A compact set K without Markov's property such that the corresponding Whitney space has the extension operator.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of compacts without Markov's property but with the extension property establishes the zone of uncertainty, but no boundary characterization is given.
